    are $u^{l_1,d}_{j_1} \otimes 
        u^{l_2,d}_{j_2} \otimes 
        \ldots

        u^{l_N,d}_{j_N} 
        \otimes u^{L,d}_{j}$

issues.failure_explanation: Because of the transpose on the last factor in eq:Mp, the last tensor factor must be an eigenvector of $(\vrho{L,\dd}{})^T$, i.e. a left eigenvector of $\vrho{L,\dd}{}$, whereas the proposition uses the right eigenvectors $u^{L,d}_j$ of $\vrho{L,\dd}{}$ itself; it also silently assumes each $\vrho{l,d}{}$ is diagonalizable. For a non-normal (e.g. defective) $\vrho{L,\dd}{}$ the displayed family neither lies in nor spans $\ker(M_d)$: e.g. $N=1$, $\vrho{l_1,d}{}=[1]$, $\vrho{L,d}{}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$ gives $\ker(M_d)=\F\otimes e_2$ while the claimed family is $\F\otimes e_1$. In the paper's actual setting (unitary representations of a compact group) the $\vrho{l,d}{}$ are skew-Hermitian, hence normal and diagonalizable, and left eigenvectors are conjugates of right eigenvectors, so the claim holds there; but as stated for general $\calL$ and $G$ it is false.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the spanning family with the last factor replaced by left eigenvectors of $\vrho{L,\dd}{}$ (equivalently eigenvectors of $(\vrho{L,\dd}{})^T$) under the same eigenvalue-sum condition, and note that skew-Hermiticity of the $\vrho{l,d}{}$ in the compact-group setting guarantees diagonalizability.
issues.overall_effect: Only the auxiliary Proposition prop:kernel_sum is affected; it is never invoked in any proof (the text presents it merely as an alternative to prop:GE_basis for determining the kernel), so no downstream result is unreliable.
issues.title: Kernel spanning claim uses right eigenvectors of the last factor instead of left eigenvectors, and assumes diagonalizability
issues.why_classification: Short local correction of the eigenvector statement; the proposition is unused downstream and its intended content is valid in the paper's setting (compact groups, skew-Hermitian generators).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, the dimension of $\bV^\bl$ is $\card{\oMl}$.

issues.failure_explanation: When $\bl^{(1)}$ and $\bl^{(2)}$ share a value, the permutation stabilizer is nontrivial and the permutation invariance couples the two blocks, so $\bV^\bl$ is a proper subspace of $\bV^{\bl^{(1)}}\otimes\bV^{\bl^{(2)}}$; e.g. for $\bl=(l,l)$ with $l\ge1$, $\dim\bV^{(l,l)}=\binom{2+2l}{2l}=(l+1)(2l+1)<(2l+1)^2=\dim(\bV^{(l)}\otimes\bV^{(l)})$. The asserted equality is therefore false. The proposition's actual conclusion, that the recursively assembled family is only a spanning set of $\bV^{\bl,L}$ in the intersecting case, remains correct, because the inclusion $\bV^\bl\subseteq\bV^{\bl^{(1)}}\otimes\bV^{\bl^{(2)}}$ together with the direct-sum decomposition of the (group-stable) tensor-product space still yields the spanning property.

issues.overall_effect: Only the justification of the spanning-set claim in the intersecting case of prop:GEPI_rec is affected; the statement of the proposition and the basis/dimension formula in the non-intersecting case are unchanged.
issues.title: Proof asserts the false equality V^bl = V^{bl1} tensor V^{bl2} in the intersecting case
issues.why_classification: One-line correction of an intermediate false equality; the proposition's statement, its basis guarantee in the non-intersecting case, and the SVD fallback all survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The closed form eq:explicit_dim_GE has lower binomial index $N-2$, which equals $-1$ when $N=1$; with the standard convention $\binom{n}{-1}=0$ every term vanishes and the formula yields $\dimge{(l)}{L}=0$ for all $L$, whereas the correct value is $\dimge{(l)}{L}=1$ if $L=l$ and $0$ otherwise (from eq:dim_su2, $\dimge{(l)}{L}=\card{\calM_{(l),L}}-\card{\calM_{(l),L+1}}$). The proof's Pascal-identity step is valid only for $N\ge2$, and the case $N=1$ is not excluded from the statement. For all $N\ge2$ the formula is correct (it reproduces the Clebsch--Gordan dimension for $N=2$ and agrees with the recursion).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to $N\ge2$, or add the trivial $N=1$ value $\dimge{(l)}{L}=\delta_{L,l}$; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit dimension formula eq:explicit_dim_GE is wrong in the degenerate case $N=1$; all uses in the paper involve $N\ge2$ (recursive formulas, asymptotics, tables), so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: Explicit GE dimension formula fails in the degenerate case N=1
issues.why_classification: Fixing a degenerate boundary case with a one-line restriction; the formula and all its uses for $N\ge2$ survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $H_4(x) = x^4-6x^2+3$ stands for the Hermite polynomial of order $4$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the stated hypothesis $L\ll\sqrt{\textup{Var}_\bl}$ (which permits, e.g., $L=\Nat^{1/4}$), the two displayed estimates are unjustified: since $H_4'(x)=4x^3-12x$, for $x=L/\sqrt{\textup{Var}_\bl}\ll1$ one has $H_4(L/\sqrt{\textup{Var}_\bl})-H_4((L+1)/\sqrt{\textup{Var}_\bl})=O(L/\textup{Var}_\bl)=O(L/\Nat)$, and $\exp(-L^2/2\textup{Var}_\bl)-\exp(-(L+1)^2/2\textup{Var}_\bl)=\frac{2L+1}{2\textup{Var}_\bl}+O(L^2/\textup{Var}_\bl^2)$; both remainders are $O(\Nat^{-1})$ (respectively $O(\Nat^{-2})$) only when $L$ is bounded. Consequently the error term $O(\Nat^{-5/2})$ in eq:dimge-est is not established for growing $L$; the argument actually yields $O(L\,\Nat^{-5/2})$. The leading asymptotic term is unaffected.

failure_location.quote:
Noting that for $L\ll \sqrt{\textup{Var}_{\bl}}$
\[
    H_4 \left(\frac{L}{\sqrt{\textup{Var}_{\bl}}} \right) - H_4 \left(\frac{L+1}{\sqrt{\textup{Var}_{\bl}}}\right) = O\left(\frac{1}{N}\right),
\]
and 
\[
    \exp\left(\frac{-L^2}{2\textup{Var}_{\bl}}\right) -  \exp\left(\frac{-(L+1)^2}{2\textup{Var}_{\bl}}\right)
    = 
    \frac{2L+1}{2\textup{Var}_{\bl}} + O\left(\frac{1}{N^2}\right), 
\]
we easily obtain~\eqref{eq:dimge-est}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either strengthen the hypothesis to bounded $L$ (e.g. $L=O(1)$), or weaken the error term to $O(L\,\Nat^{-5/2})$ (resp. $O(L\,\Nb^{-5/2})$ in prop:asym-dim-gepi); the leading asymptotic is preserved either way.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised uniform error rate $O(\Nat^{-5/2})$ (and its multi-block analogue $O(\Nb^{-5/2})$ in prop:asym-dim-gepi, whose proof is the same one-line sketch and hits the same gap) is unsubstantiated for growing $L$; the main asymptotic term, the linear-in-$L$ scaling, the PI vs GE-PI comparability conclusion, and the fixed-$L$ numerical error analysis all remain valid.
issues.title: The O(Nat^{-5/2}) error term is not supported under the hypothesis L << sqrt(Var); the proof requires bounded L
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained hypothesis/rate adjustment avoiding new proof architecture, but it necessarily withdraws the uniformly advertised error rate, a stated guarantee of the proposition; the main asymptotic term survives.
